items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez, White to move (the board you just saw). Tap the squares on ranks 4 to 6 (counting from White's side) that no black pawn guards now and none can ever guard. There are two.

claims.statement: Black has exactly two holes, a5 and c6.

hints: Look at the pawns that have already moved past a square: b5 and d6.
A black pawn guards the two squares diagonally in front of it, toward rank 1: a pawn on b6 would guard a5 and c5.
The two squares are on the a-file and the c-file.
items.explain: The pawn on b5 has moved past a5, and c6 lies between the pawns on b5 and d6, which have both moved beyond it. No black pawn can ever guard either square. A hole is a fact about pawns only; it matters when an enemy piece can use the square.

items.prompt: Same position. White also has one hole on its 3rd to 5th ranks. Tap it.

claims.statement: White's only hole is d3.

hints: Which white pawns have moved forward from their start squares?
The pawns on c3 and e4 stand on both sides of a square.
The square is on the third rank.
items.explain: A pawn on c2 or e2 could guard d3, but those pawns have moved to c3 and e4. So no white pawn can ever guard d3.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: Black has just played ...c5 and the pawn on d4 is attacked twice. White to move. Find a sound move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
The engine rates dxc5 at least 70 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).
After dxc5 Nxc5 the knight on c5 attacks the bishop on b3.

hints: Count the pieces attacking d4 and the pieces defending it.
If a capture changes the structure, ask who recaptures and with what.
Moving a piece to a better square keeps d4 protected.
items.explain: The pawn on d4 is attacked by two pawns and defended by a pawn and a knight, so White need not capture. If White takes on c5, the knight on d7 recaptures with an attack on the bishop on b3. Bc2, Nf1 and d5 are the plans this lesson looks at; several quiet moves are also within 40 centipawns of the engine's best (depth 16).

feedback_by_move.d4c5: At depth 16 the engine rates dxc5 at least 70 centipawns below the best move: after Nxc5 the knight attacks the bishop and White has spent the d4 pawn for nothing.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: White has built the pawns on e4 and d4 and played Nbd2. Black to move. Find a move that keeps the tension in the centre without capturing.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After c5 two black pawns attack d4.

hints: Black does not have to capture on d4 to put d4 under pressure.
Which pawn move attacks d4 from the side?
A piece move that has not been made yet also keeps the tension.
items.explain: After ...c5 the pawns on c5 and e5 both attack d4. Bb7 and Rb8 develop without changing the pawns, and several waiting moves are also fine. All accepted moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move (depth 16).

feedback_by_move.e5d4: At depth 16 the engine rates exd4 clearly lower: after cxd4 White has a pawn pair on e4 and d4 and Black has nothing to attack yet.

items.prompt: Same position, Black to move. Black captures at once: exd4, and White recaptures cxd4. Who does the engine prefer then?

claims.statement: After exd4 cxd4 the engine (depth 16) rates the position at least 70 centipawns in White's favour.
The engine rates exd4 at least 60 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).

hints: Think about which pawns stand in the centre after the two captures.
Does Black have a piece that attacks d4 yet?
Count Black's central pawns and White's.
items.explain: After exd4 cxd4 White holds pawns on e4 and d4 and Black has no central pawn on the e-file or d-file that can fight back, and no piece attacks them yet. At depth 16 the engine prefers White by at least 70 centipawns.

items.prompt: Black's knight on c6 and the pawn on e5 both attack d4, and only the knight on f3 defends it. White to move. Find a move that answers the pressure.

claims.statement: Two black pieces attack d4.
One white piece defends d4.
At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After Nb3 three white pieces defend d4: both knights and the queen.

hints: Count the attackers of d4 and the defenders of d4.
One of the accepted moves adds a defender to d4.
Other sound moves prepare to meet ...Nb4 and ...exd4.
items.explain: Nb3 adds a defender of d4 and opens the d-file for the queen, so three pieces defend it. At depth 16 a3, Bd3 and several quiet moves are also within 40 centipawns of the engine's best.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez, the set-up with ...g6. White to move. Find a sensible move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After a4 the pawn on a4 attacks the pawn on b5.

hints: Look at the pawn that stands on b5.
Which white pawn can attack b5 from the side?
Developing the bishop is also fine.
items.explain: The move a4 puts a pawn against b5 and prepares axb5, the queenside lever. Bd2 and Bg5 develop the bishop, and several quiet moves are close in value. All accepted moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best (depth 16).

items.prompt: Same position, Black to move. After ...c5, how do the attackers and defenders of d4 compare?

claims.statement: After c5 two black pawns attack d4.
After c5 two white pieces defend d4.

hints: Count pawns first, then pieces.
Black's attackers after c5 are both pawns.
White defends d4 with a pawn and a knight.
items.explain: After ...c5 the pawns on c5 and e5 attack d4; the pawn on c3 and the knight on f3 defend it. Equal numbers mean that the first capture does not win a pawn; what matters is the recapture.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: White has played a4 and taken on b5. Black to move. Recapture, or do something else? Find the engine's choice.

claims.statement: At depth 16 the engine's best move is axb5.
The engine rates exd4 at least 50 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).
After axb5 the a-file holds no black pawn and no white pawn: it is open.

hints: Count the pieces: a pawn has been captured.
Which recapture keeps the pawn structure healthy?
After the recapture the a-file is open.
items.explain: The recapture axb5 restores the pawn on b5 and opens the a-file for both rooks. Other moves leave the pawn on b5 in White's hands.

feedback_by_move.e5d4: At depth 16 the engine rates exd4 at least 50 centipawns lower than axb5: White keeps the extra pawn on b5 and the tension in the centre is gone.
feedback_by_move.d8c8: Leaving the pawn on b5 is far worse than recapturing.

items.prompt: Black to move. Find a sensible move.

claims.statement: At depth 16 every accepted move is within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move.
After cxd4 cxd4 the c-file is open.

hints: Count the attackers of d4 first.
Is there a lever available that uses a queen already on the c-file?
Developing the last bishop is also fine.
items.explain: Black can use the lever at once with cxd4, or finish development first with Bd7. Several other moves are close; all accepted moves are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best (depth 16).

items.prompt: White to move. Is dxe5 (then ...dxe5) White's best move here?

claims.statement: The engine rates dxe5 at least 40 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).

hints: A capture changes the structure: who gets the tempo?
Count what each side's pieces can attack after the trade.
Compare with the quiet developing moves.
items.explain: No. After dxe5 dxe5 both sides get the open d-file, and White has given up the d4 pawn that held space and gets nothing for it. At depth 16 the engine prefers quiet moves such as a4 by around half a pawn.

items.prompt: Closed Ruy Lopez: the pawn on a4 attacks the knight on b3. White to move. Find a safe square for the knight; two moves are accepted.

claims.statement: The pawn on a4 attacks the knight on b3.
At depth 16 the engine's best move is Nbd2 or Nc1, and both are within 40 centipawns of it.
The engine rates Bd3 at least 300 centipawns lower than its best move (depth 16).

hints: The knight is attacked by a pawn: it must move or be defended in a way that does not lose it.
A bishop move that ignores the attack loses the knight.
Two knight moves are accepted.
items.explain: A pawn attack on a knight is answered by moving the knight (or by a counter-threat that is worth more). Nbd2 and Nc1 are within 40 centipawns of the engine's best move; Bd3 allows axb3 and loses at least 300 centipawns at depth 16.

feedback_by_move.c2d3: The pawn on a4 takes the knight on b3: at depth 16 the engine rates Bd3 at least 300 centipawns lower than the best move.
